passage: Leela, you asked why my portfolio still doesn't exist, so let me, Kunal, be honest. The first week I picked the font. The second week I changed the font. Then I decided the site needed a slide-in animation, and then a different one, and by the end of month one I had redesigned the top banner six times. I told myself it was not ready. Two months went by like that. Meanwhile, three of my classmates had put up plain pages and got interview calls. No one has seen my projects, not one recruiter, because there is nothing to click. I was so afraid of it being ordinary that I made it invisible. I still have not published it.

qa.q: How many times had Kunal redesigned the top banner?
qa.a: Kunal had redesigned the top banner six times.

qa.q: What was Kunal afraid of, according to the account?
qa.a: Kunal was afraid of the portfolio being ordinary, so it stayed hidden and nobody could see it.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Kunal use, and why?
qa.a: Kunal could publish a plain version this week and improve it later, because a visible page can get feedback and calls while an unpublished one cannot.

qa.q: How might Leela see Kunal's situation?
qa.a: Leela asked why the portfolio does not exist, and gets an honest answer, so Leela may see a friend whose skill is fine but who is stuck on polish.

grounding: Shows perfectionism about fonts and animations delaying a portfolio launch for months so that no recruiter ever sees the work.

passage:
I'm Payal, and I sit next to Farhan in the final-year lab. In June he told me his portfolio would go live 'this weekend'. I saw it that weekend: clean, three projects, looked good to me.
Then the fonts changed. Then they changed back. In July he spent a week on an animation where the project cards flip over when you hover. Every few days he'd turn his screen toward me: 'Better, or was the old one better?' I honestly couldn't tell the difference.
In August the placement cell asked everyone to submit portfolio links. Farhan submitted his old college profile page instead. I watched him close the laptop harder than usual.
The portfolio is still sitting on his machine, now with a loading animation, and as far as I know no recruiter has seen it.

qa.q: What did Farhan submit to the placement cell instead of the portfolio?
What might Farhan have been feeling when he closed the laptop harder than usual?
qa.a: He may have felt frustrated with himself and embarrassed, since two months of polishing still left nothing to submit.

qa.q: What would you change first in Farhan's approach?
qa.a: Publish the June version as it was and improve the fonts and animations after it is live, so recruiters see something while it gets better.

qa.q: What is it like for Payal to be asked 'Better, or was the old one better?'
qa.a: Payal can't tell the difference and may feel helpless, watching a friend polish something that already looked good.

grounding: Shows a student redesigning fonts and animations for two months and never publishing, so no recruiter sees the work.

passage:
October, first week. Bhavna finishes three projects and starts her portfolio site. She picks a font. By Sunday she has swapped it four times. 'It has to look professional,' she tells her sister Salma.
November, a Tuesday. Salma finds her at midnight adjusting how fast the header fades in. The contact page is still blank. A friend's internship form closed that morning; Bhavna didn't apply because 'the site isn't ready'.
December, a Saturday. A senior from her college posts that his company is hiring juniors and wants portfolio links by Monday. Bhavna opens the site. The animations are smooth. Two project pages still say 'coming soon'. She sends the senior nothing, and sits on the bed looking at the message for a long time.

qa.q: How many times did Bhavna swap the font in the first week?
What was Bhavna likely feeling as she sat looking at the senior's message?
qa.a: She was likely regretful and discouraged, watching another chance pass because the site still felt unfinished to her.

qa.q: What small step could Bhavna take even on that Saturday?
qa.a: Hide the 'coming soon' pages, publish the finished project and the contact page, and send the link by Monday.

qa.q: How might Salma see these two months?
qa.a: Salma likely feels worried, watching her sister lose chances over things like fade speed while the important pages stay empty.

grounding: Shows perfectionism over fonts and animations stretching over two months, with missed applications and no recruiter ever seeing the site.
